pack_metadata.title: Import and legally sell a first regulated product shipment in India
pack_metadata.user_outcome: An Indian importer can identify and complete the central-government and necessary regulated-actor steps for a first commercial import, obtain customs release, and hold sale until every applicable product, tax, packaging and environmental gate has evidence.
pack_metadata.central_scope: Product-neutral Central Government graph covering importer identity, DGFT import policy, customs classification/valuation/filing/payment/release, conditional national product regulators, nationwide portals, GST, packaged-commodity and environmental obligations, and necessary regulated/private actors. State and local dependencies are surfaced but not invented.
explicit_exclusions: No tariff code, duty rate, exemption, anti-dumping or safeguard measure is declared for an unidentified product or incomplete shipment facts.
No state, municipal, premises, fire, trade, professional-tax, state-excise or local retail procedure is invented.
No private carrier, customs-broker, laboratory or bank price or service-level promise is asserted.
No approval is inferred from a portal submission, payment, shipment arrival or customs Out of Charge alone.
This pack does not replace a binding customs classification ruling, regulator decision, legal advice, laboratory result or customs assessment.

qualifying_questions.question: What is the exact product, model, technical construction, principal function, materials, intended use and retail presentation?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Tariff classification, import policy, regulator scope, standards, labelling and waste obligations turn on objective product facts, not a marketing name.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: If the model-level technical dossier is incomplete, do not finalise classification, regulatory scope, duty, label artwork, shipment dispatch or sale release.

qualifying_questions.question: Is the shipment new finished goods, components, samples, used/refurbished goods, waste/scrap, or goods for repair/re-export?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Import policy, authorisations, testing, waste rules and possible exemptions differ materially by condition and purpose.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Unknown, used, waste or special-purpose status blocks the ordinary commercial-sale path until the exact DGFT and regulator conditions are verified.

qualifying_questions.question: Does the product intentionally transmit or receive radio, and what are every frequency band, power, modulation, module and antenna configuration?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: WPC spectrum authorisation, equipment type approval, import authorisation and possible telecom certification depend on exact radio characteristics.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: If radio specifications or current licence-exempt-band evidence are missing, do not import or sell the radio-enabled product.

qualifying_questions.question: Is the product notified telecom equipment, network equipment, terminal equipment, or only a consumer accessory?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Notified telecom equipment may require MTCTE conformity assessment before sale, deployment or use.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: A 'not sure' answer requires checking the current MTCTE notified product list and essential requirements before dispatch.

qualifying_questions.question: Does the product contain or constitute food, drug, cosmetic, medical device, plant/seed, animal product, wildlife material, chemical, pesticide, hazardous material, ozone-depleting substance, fuel/gas/pressure equipment, energy-labelled equipment, or another specially regulated article?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: These traits can trigger a different competent Central regulator, import permit, inspection, NOC, designated port or prohibition.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Any selected or uncertain trait blocks dispatch until the competent regulator, permit/NOC route, port condition and evidence are identified.

qualifying_questions.question: Does the product or shipment contain a battery, electrical/electronic equipment, plastic packaging, or another material covered by an EPR/waste regime?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Importer/producer registration, EPR, RoHS, record and downstream recycler obligations can arise before business or sale.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Unknown scope or missing applicable EPR registration blocks sale; do not infer coverage or exemption from product description alone.

qualifying_questions.question: Will the product be imported or sold in a package made before the buyer is present, and what declarations and retail channels are planned?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: Packaged-commodity registration and declarations can apply to imported retail packages and online listings.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: If packaged-commodity applicability or label content is unresolved, quarantine stock and do not offer it for sale.

qualifying_questions.question: What Indian legal entity will be importer of record, and does its PAN, bank account, IEC, GSTIN, addresses and authorised signatory data match across systems?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: DGFT and ICEGATE identity, customs filing, tax and regulator accounts depend on the actual Indian entity and matching records.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: No entity or mismatched identity means no filing under assumed credentials; correct source systems first.

qualifying_questions.question: What are origin, export country, supplier/manufacturer, quantity, unit, Incoterm, currency, invoice price, assists/royalties/packing/freight/insurance, payment terms, route and intended Indian port?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: These facts drive customs value, origin/preferences, trade remedies, DGFT authorisation fields, routing, designated-port conditions and filing documents.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Incomplete commercial or route facts prevent final duty, preference, trade-remedy, port and filing conclusions.

qualifying_questions.question: What current ITC(HS) code and policy condition has been supported by the product facts, and is the item Free, Restricted, Prohibited, STE/canalised, subject to a port condition, or uncertain?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: A marketing name or supplier code is not enough to decide whether import is permitted or which authorisation is needed.
options: Free with no special condition found
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Uncertain, restricted, prohibited or conditional policy blocks shipment dispatch until resolved; prohibited goods have no ordinary happy path.

qualifying_questions.question: Where will goods be imported, stored and supplied; is the importer GST-registered; and are supplies intra-State, inter-State, marketplace, wholesale, retail or e-commerce?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: GST registration, place-of-supply, invoicing, return and state/local dependencies depend on the actual business model and locations.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Do not quote a GST rate, issue an invoice or claim import IGST credit until registration and supply facts are verified.

qualifying_questions.question: For each claimed licence or registration, do the certificate holder, Indian representative, manufacturer/factory, brand, model, standard, validity and conditions match this shipment?
qualifying_questions.why_it_matters: A certificate for another entity, factory, model or standard is not shipment-level clearance evidence.
qualifying_questions.blocking_logic: Any scope mismatch, expiry, suspension or unverifiable record blocks dispatch and sale.

tasks.title: Create the model-level product and shipment evidence dossier
tasks.user_goal: Replace a marketing description with the technical, commercial and intended-use facts needed to classify and regulate the exact shipment.
tasks.trigger: Before purchase order, regulator application, label printing or shipment dispatch.
steps: Record exact model, construction, principal function, materials, intended use, condition, components, accessories, power source and package configuration.
Collect model-specific manuals, BOM, photographs, radio specifications and existing certificates directly from the manufacturer.
Record supplier, manufacturer/factory, origin, quantity, value elements, Incoterm, route and intended port.
Answer every qualifying question; record unknowns as blockers rather than assumptions.
tasks.tracking: Use a versioned dossier tied to model, purchase order, supplier and shipment reference; log every later correction.
tasks.rejection_handling: Return incomplete or inconsistent evidence to the supplier/manufacturer; do not substitute generic web specifications.
tasks.escalation: Escalate unresolved technical facts to the manufacturer and classification/regulatory specialists before committing shipment.

state_local_dependency.description: The evidence dossier is product and shipment specific; later questions identify location dependencies.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A dossier is complete only as user evidence; it does not itself prove tariff or regulator scope.

tasks.title: Obtain or verify the Importer-Exporter Code
tasks.user_goal: Ensure the actual Indian importer can lawfully use its DGFT identity for the shipment.
tasks.trigger: The importer intends to make a commercial import and no verified active IEC is on file.

fees_duties.label: IEC application/update fee
fees_duties.applicability: Current exact fee was not established in admitted source text; inspect the live DGFT application before payment.

timelines.label: Processing time
timelines.applicability: No current guaranteed processing time was admitted.

steps: On the DGFT site choose Apply for IEC or Update IEC and use the actual importer entity.
Enter matching entity, PAN, address, contact, incorporation/constitution and bank information; complete portal authentication and declarations.
Download the e-IEC certificate and independently verify its displayed particulars through DGFT's IEC view facility.
tasks.tracking: Track the DGFT application/reference in the importer compliance register and recheck particulars before each filing.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct the authoritative PAN, bank, corporate, GST or signatory record that caused mismatch and resubmit through DGFT.
tasks.escalation: Use the DGFT portal grievance/help route for an unresolved application; do not create a second IEC for the same entity as a workaround.

state_local_dependency.description: IEC is a central DGFT identity; the entity may separately need state/local business permissions.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Do not file using another entity's IEC or an IEC whose identity does not match the importer of record.

tasks.title: Create and validate the ICEGATE customs account
tasks.user_goal: Give the importer or authorised customs filer a matched, authenticated channel for customs services.
tasks.trigger: Before document upload, Bill of Entry filing or customs payment/status access.
steps: Use ICEGATE Registration and select the appropriate importer/trade role.
Match organisation, PAN, IEC and contact data to DGFT/GSTN records and complete the current digital authentication flow.
If a GSTIN is used, confirm its current IEC mapping through the service listed on ICEGATE.
Test login and retain only account references, never credentials, in the dossier.
tasks.tracking: Use ICEGATE's logged-in dashboard and registration reference; revalidate credentials and mappings before filing.
tasks.rejection_handling: Resolve source-system identity mismatch rather than repeatedly uploading altered copies.
tasks.escalation: Use ICEGATE Helpdesk with the reference ID and non-secret error evidence; Customs Service Centre is a filing-access fallback, not identity approval.

state_local_dependency.description: ICEGATE is nationwide; GST registration itself can depend on State/UT facts.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A registered portal account is not product approval, import permission or customs release.

tasks.title: Determine tariff classification and current DGFT import policy
tasks.user_goal: Establish a supportable ITC(HS)/customs classification and whether import is free, restricted, prohibited or conditional.
tasks.trigger: A complete model-level dossier exists and before quote acceptance, authorisation or dispatch.
steps: Apply the tariff text, section/chapter notes and objective product facts to create a reasoned classification record.
Check the live DGFT ITC(HS) policy entry, policy conditions, notifications and any port/end-use condition for the proposed code.
Use ICEGATE CIP/tariff tools as discovery/calculation aids, not as a substitute for authoritative legal text or a binding ruling.
If two headings remain plausible or the consequence is material, obtain a qualified opinion or pursue a binding customs ruling route before dispatch.
tasks.tracking: Version the analysis with the exact tariff edition, notifications, product evidence and review date.
tasks.rejection_handling: On customs disagreement, preserve the assessment/query, respond with technical evidence and use the applicable review/appeal route rather than silently changing codes.
tasks.escalation: Escalate ambiguity to a customs classification specialist and, where appropriate, the statutory advance-ruling route.

state_local_dependency.description: Tariff and DGFT policy are central; product sale may still be subject to State/UT controls.

tasks.fail_closed_note: No numeric duty, policy status or authorisation conclusion may be reused across models without a current classification record.

tasks.title: Seek a customs advance ruling when classification ambiguity is material
tasks.user_goal: Obtain an authoritative classification determination before the first shipment when competing headings cannot safely be resolved from the product record.
tasks.trigger: A material classification question remains after applying the tariff text and objective model facts, and the importer elects or is advised to seek an advance ruling.

fees_duties.label: CAAR application fee
fees_duties.applicability: No current exact amount is asserted from the admitted source; check Form CAAR-1 and the receiving authority before submission.

steps: Identify the jurisdictional Customs Authority for Advance Rulings from the applicant address under regulation 6.
Prepare Form CAAR-1 with the complete product, proposed transaction, classification question, legal analysis and supporting technical evidence.
Submit by the current official route and retain the receiving acknowledgement and every requisition/response.

Do not dispatch on a pending request where the unresolved classification changes admissibility, authorisation, duty or product-regulator treatment; apply the final ruling only within its actual applicant/fact scope.
tasks.tracking: Track the CAAR acknowledgement, authority, questions, hearings and signed ruling against the exact product dossier version.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct an incomplete filing only through the authority's stated process; do not treat non-admission or a ruling for different facts as classification proof.
tasks.escalation: Use the jurisdictional CAAR contact and qualified customs counsel for an unresolved filing or material change in facts.

state_local_dependency.description: Advance ruling on customs classification is a Central customs route.

tasks.fail_closed_note: This route exists, but a pending application does not fix the case classification and a ruling cannot be transplanted to a materially different product or transaction.

tasks.title: Resolve customs value, origin, preference, trade remedies and duty case
tasks.user_goal: Calculate a shipment-specific customs exposure without hiding unknown rates, additions or origin conditions.
tasks.trigger: A candidate tariff classification and complete commercial facts are available.

fees_duties.label: Basic customs duty and applicable cesses/levies
fees_duties.applicability: Requires exact classification, date, origin, notifications, value additions and trade-remedy review.

fees_duties.label: Import IGST
fees_duties.applicability: Rate and amount require the classified goods, like-article GST rate, customs value and applicable duties.

steps: Document related-party status, consideration, assists, royalties, commissions, packing, freight, insurance and other value elements.
Verify non-preferential origin and, only if claimed, the exact preferential rule, certificate/data and direct-transport conditions.
Check current tariff notifications, exemptions, anti-dumping, safeguard and countervailing measures for the classification/origin/date.
Prepare a line-by-line calculation and reconcile it to the customs assessment; leave each unsupported number blank.
tasks.tracking: Retain dated sources and calculation versions; separately record customs-assessed amounts and paid challan.
tasks.rejection_handling: If customs rejects value, origin or benefit, respond with transaction/origin evidence and pay or contest only through the lawful assessment/review route.
tasks.escalation: Escalate related-party, royalty, origin or trade-remedy uncertainty to qualified customs/tax counsel before dispatch.

state_local_dependency.description: Import valuation and border duties are central; post-import supplies have separate State/UT GST facts.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Duty calculators are estimates; only current legal inputs and the shipment assessment support payment and landed-cost claims.

tasks.title: Obtain DGFT import authorisation or stop the restricted path
tasks.user_goal: Do not dispatch goods whose policy status requires a DGFT permission that has not been granted for the actual goods and shipment.
tasks.trigger: The current DGFT policy entry or condition identifies the goods as restricted or otherwise requires an import authorisation.

fees_duties.label: DGFT authorisation application fee
fees_duties.applicability: Exact current fee was not admitted and must be checked in the live application.

timelines.label: Authorisation processing time
timelines.applicability: No guaranteed current time was admitted.

steps: Use DGFT Services > Import Management System > Import Authorization for Restricted Imports > Apply for New Authorization.
Supply the exact ITC(HS), technical description/specification, quantity/UOM, CIF value, country, port, purpose and justification plus required sector documents.
Wait for a granted authorisation and verify quantity, value, goods, validity, port and conditions against the proposed shipment.
tasks.tracking: Track portal application/reference and utilisation against licence quantity/value/validity.
tasks.rejection_handling: Do not dispatch on a pending or rejected application; correct evidence or use the stated review/grievance route.
tasks.escalation: Escalate a policy ambiguity to DGFT and qualified trade counsel; prohibited goods remain blocked absent an express lawful route.

state_local_dependency.description: DGFT authorisation is central but may coexist with sector and State/UT permissions.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A submitted application, payment or prior licence for other goods is not authorisation for this shipment.

tasks.title: Build and close the applicable Central regulator matrix
tasks.user_goal: Identify every national product, safety, spectrum, telecom, environment, packaged-commodity and sector gate before dispatch.
tasks.trigger: Before purchase commitment, testing, licence filing or shipment dispatch.
steps: Map each product trait and intended use to current QCO/standard, spectrum, telecom, waste/EPR, packaged-commodity and sector rules.

For food, drug/device/cosmetic, plant/seed, animal, wildlife, chemical/hazardous, ODS, fuel/gas/pressure/explosive and energy-labelled traits, identify the competent authority and exact current notification.
Record applicability, exemption, required approval, certificate scope, port condition, filing route and proof as separate atomic conclusions.
Route each positive or uncertain branch to its specialist task; unresolved scope remains a shipment blocker.
tasks.tracking: Date every row and link the operative notification, model evidence and approval proof.
tasks.rejection_handling: Reopen the matrix when a regulator, customs officer or lab identifies an unrecorded trait or scope mismatch.
tasks.escalation: Ask the competent authority for written clarification or seek specialist counsel when the official product list/notification does not resolve scope.

state_local_dependency.description: The central matrix must flag genuine State/UT licensing, premises and sale controls, but task imp.t19 resolves them by location.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A list of common regulators is not exhaustive evidence for an unidentified product; 'no approval required' must be reasoned and sourced.

tasks.title: Obtain or verify BIS conformity evidence when in scope
tasks.user_goal: Ensure a product subject to a QCO/compulsory scheme is covered by the correct current BIS licence or registration before import and sale.
tasks.trigger: The exact product/standard appears in a current QCO or compulsory-certification list, or scope is unresolved.

fees_duties.label: Scheme-II application fee
fees_duties.applicability: Each Scheme-II application under the substituted 2026 Scheme II.

fees_duties.label: Scheme-II annual licence fee
fees_duties.applicability: Annual licence fee under the substituted 2026 Scheme II.

fees_duties.label: Scheme-II renewal application fee
fees_duties.applicability: Renewal application under the substituted 2026 Scheme II.

fees_duties.label: Scheme-II yearly processing fee
fees_duties.applicability: Payable yearly in advance for grant and continuation; statutory concessions depend on applicant category/date and are not calculated here.

fees_duties.label: Additional Scheme-II test report
fees_duties.value: INR 20,000 for each additional test report
fees_duties.applicability: Only when the application contains more than one test report.

fees_duties.label: Scheme-II inclusion of new varieties/models or scope extension
fees_duties.applicability: Only for an inclusion or scope-extension application.

fees_duties.label: Third-party laboratory testing and surveillance sample costs
fees_duties.applicability: The regulation allocates testing/sample costs but does not establish one universal laboratory amount for this model.

timelines.label: Initial Scheme-II licence validity
timelines.applicability: A granted Scheme-II licence; exact granted dates are those in Form V.

timelines.label: Scheme-II renewal period
timelines.value: Up to a further five years
timelines.applicability: A renewal granted under current Scheme II.

timelines.label: Application processing time
timelines.applicability: The 2026 regulations do not establish a universal application turnaround for this product.

steps: Determine the applicable BIS scheme, QCO, Indian Standard and implementation date for the exact model.

For Scheme II, the manufacturer identifies the product, Indian Standard/essential requirements, manufacturing/testing capability, model and brand, then applies separately for each product in Form I and generally separately for each brand.

Submit the Form II undertaking, third-party laboratory test report, applicable Form III affidavit and, for a foreign manufacturer, the Form IV Indian-representative nomination; treat only a BIS grant in Form V as the licence.
For a foreign manufacturer under a non-CRS compulsory scheme, use the current FMCS/Manakonline route and valid Authorised Indian Representative arrangement.
Verify registration/licence status, manufacturer/factory, brand, model, standard, validity and marking against the shipment before dispatch and sale.
tasks.tracking: Search the public CRS record by registration/product/model/status/validity/brand and monitor expiry, suspension, cancellation and scope change by model and factory.
tasks.rejection_handling: Route any suspended, cancelled, expired or scope-mismatched record to task imp.t08a; quarantine non-covered goods and correct model/factory evidence, retest/reapply, or follow a lawful authority-directed disposition.
tasks.escalation: Use registration@bis.gov.in for CRS support and the published DDG (Registration) grievance channel when support does not resolve the case; the 2026 amendment controls the Scheme-II form, evidence, fee, validity, suspension and cancellation points stated here.

state_local_dependency.description: BIS is national; local enforcement and premises controls may coexist.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A laboratory report, application receipt or certificate for another factory/model is not BIS coverage.

tasks.title: Resolve a BIS suspension, cancellation, expiry or scope mismatch
tasks.user_goal: Prevent import or sale on a BIS record that no longer authorises the exact product and restore only authority-backed coverage.
tasks.trigger: The public/issued BIS record is suspended, cancelled, expired, under notice, or does not cover the actual factory, brand, model or standard.

timelines.label: Notice before Scheme-II suspension or cancellation
timelines.applicability: A notice under the 2026 Scheme-II suspension/cancellation provision; act on the actual notice date and content.

steps: Preserve the public status, BIS notice/order and exact licence/model scope; stop importing, marking and selling affected stock.
Within the notice process, submit the manufacturer/laboratory/corrective evidence requested by BIS and track the official decision.
After cancellation, do not supply, import, distribute or sell goods under that licence and remove/stop use of the Standard Mark as directed by the regulation.
Release stock only after a current Form V/public record or written BIS decision affirmatively covers the exact goods.
tasks.tracking: Retain the public search capture, notice, response acknowledgement, BIS order and restored licence/scope record.
tasks.rejection_handling: A support ticket or grievance does not stay a suspension/cancellation or reinstate scope; continue the hold until BIS evidence does so.
tasks.escalation: Use CRS support at registration@bis.gov.in, then the published DDG (Registration) grievance contact with the registration/application reference and non-secret evidence.

state_local_dependency.description: The BIS licence remedy is Central; local enforcement action may still need its own response.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Pending correspondence, past status or a supplier assurance cannot restore a suspended, cancelled, expired or mismatched BIS licence.

tasks.title: Resolve WPC spectrum and wireless equipment authorisations
tasks.user_goal: Import and sell radio equipment only after its bands, emissions, approval and current filing route are proven.
tasks.trigger: The product intentionally transmits/receives radio or contains a radio module.

fees_duties.label: WPC authorisation/ETA fee
fees_duties.applicability: The public ETA page states a figure, but the authorisation route migrated in 2026; reverify the applicable service and live fee before payment.

timelines.label: WPC processing time/validity
timelines.applicability: Do not rely on legacy portal language after the 2026 transition without written confirmation.

steps: List every radio band, power, modulation, antenna and module and match it to current spectrum rules/notifications.
Determine whether ETA/self-declaration, REPA, an exception under rule 10, or another spectrum/equipment authorisation applies to the exact configuration and purpose.
Use accredited model-specific test evidence and manufacturer authority for the Indian applicant where required.
Confirm the post-June-2026 ETA application route in writing; separately route any REPA question to task imp.t09a, whose current public route and statutory exceptions are verified.
tasks.tracking: Track the current authorisation portal record and retain the operative frequency notification, test report and certificate together.
tasks.rejection_handling: Do not import on a legacy receipt or assumed licence exemption; correct the technical/configuration evidence or stop the radio path.
tasks.escalation: Obtain written WPC/DoT route confirmation because official pages conflict after the Telecommunications Act authorisation migration.

state_local_dependency.description: Spectrum authorisation is central; site-specific deployments may create other approvals outside this first-product sale graph.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Licence-exempt spectrum does not mean the equipment, import or sale is automatically approval-exempt.

tasks.title: Obtain Radio Equipment Possession Authorisation or prove a rule 10 exception
tasks.user_goal: Import radio equipment for sale only with the current REPA grant or an exact statutory exception that actually permits the intended commercial activity.
tasks.trigger: The importer proposes to import radio equipment for sale/hire/test/demo and no exact rule 10 exception has yet been proven.

fees_duties.label: REPA application fee
fees_duties.applicability: Each application under rule 4(4).

fees_duties.label: REPA annual authorisation fee for manufacture/purchase/import for sale or hire
fees_duties.applicability: Letter-of-intent route for rule 4(1)(a)-(c); use the actual LoI.

fees_duties.label: REPA authorisation fee for repair/test/demo
fees_duties.value: INR 2,000 per annum; proportionate for a shorter period subject to INR 500 minimum
fees_duties.applicability: Rule 4(1)(d)-(f), subject to the exact period and LoI.

timelines.label: REPA validity
timelines.value: One to five years for manufacture/purchase/import for sale or hire; up to twelve months for repair/test/demo
timelines.applicability: Exact grant period is stated in the authorisation.

steps: Match the importer, activity, make, model and quantity to rule 4 and test every rule 10 exception against the exact licence/authorisation/exemption facts.
Do not use the end-user/subscriber exception for a commercial importer or seller; the rule states that excepted persons cannot manufacture, sell or hire the equipment.

If no exception applies, apply through DoT's Radio Equipment Possession Authorisation service, upload entity/authorisation and radio-equipment details, and pay only against the official application/LoI.
Retain the granted authorisation and verify activity, make/model, quantity, validity and conditions before dispatch and sale.
tasks.tracking: Use the Authorisation Portal View Status route and retain the application, LoI/payment and grant; monitor quantity and validity.
tasks.rejection_handling: On rejection or a request for information, preserve the portal order, correct only the requested evidence and keep import/sale blocked.
tasks.escalation: Raise a ticket through the current DoT service page/helpdesk with the application reference; obtain written WPC/DoT confirmation for a disputed exception.

state_local_dependency.description: REPA is a Central telecommunications authorisation.

tasks.fail_closed_note: An ETA, licence-exempt frequency or end-user exception does not by itself prove that a commercial importer may possess/import the equipment for sale.

tasks.title: Obtain MTCTE certification when the equipment is notified
tasks.user_goal: Prevent import/sale/deployment of notified telecom equipment without model-level conformity evidence.
tasks.trigger: The exact product is within the current MTCTE notified product/essential-requirement scope or that scope is uncertain.

fees_duties.label: MTCTE testing/application fee
fees_duties.applicability: Exact product category, certification scheme and current portal determine cost.

steps: Check the live MTCTE notified products and essential requirements against the exact model and intended use.
Where applicable, register the eligible Indian applicant/AIR, complete testing and submit the current portal application.
Verify certificate model, brand, OEM, applicant/AIR, validity and conditions before import/sale/deployment.
tasks.tracking: Monitor certificate and notification changes on the MTCTE portal by product and model.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct scope/test evidence or stop sale/deployment; do not use absence from an old list as proof of exemption.
tasks.escalation: Seek TEC clarification when consumer-accessory versus notified telecom-equipment scope is unclear.

state_local_dependency.description: MTCTE is national; network/site permissions are outside this bounded goods-import graph.

tasks.fail_closed_note: WPC approval and BIS conformity do not substitute for MTCTE where MTCTE is independently applicable.

tasks.title: Complete battery, e-waste and packaging EPR branches
tasks.user_goal: Register the importer/producer and establish waste-stream compliance before placing covered products or packaging on the market.
tasks.trigger: The importer places a battery, equipment containing a battery, Schedule-I EEE or regulated plastic packaging/other EPR material on the Indian market.

fees_duties.label: EPR registration/application charges
fees_duties.applicability: Waste stream, category, turnover/quantity and current portal determine charges; no universal amount is supplied.

steps: Map product and packaging to the current schedules/categories separately for battery, e-waste, plastic and any other EPR stream.
For equipment containing a battery, complete the applicable producer registration on CPCB's battery EPR portal before business and retain the certificate.
For EEE, verify Schedule-I coverage and RoHS/EPR obligations; when supported continue to task imp.t11b, not from generic electronics language.
For plastic packaging, complete the BOM/PIBO assessment and continue to task imp.t11c when applicable; the current route is CPCB's Common EPR Portal.
Establish collection/recycling, certificate, return, record and supplier-data controls required by each applicable regime.
For any in-scope battery or equipment containing a battery, continue to task imp.t11a; producer registration alone does not prove the required registration-number marking on the sale lot.
tasks.tracking: Maintain registration status, targets, purchases/transfers, returns and recycler/refurbisher evidence by waste stream and year.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct entity/category/quantity evidence and portal objections; quarantine sale stock while required registration is absent.
tasks.escalation: Ask CPCB for scope/portal clarification where the Schedule or migrated portal does not resolve the exact product/role.

state_local_dependency.description: Central producer registration can coexist with State Pollution Control Board permissions for facilities/recyclers; do not infer those procedures here.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A recycler contract or portal account is not the importer's producer registration, and the registration certificate is not physical battery marking proof; uncertain Schedule mapping remains Action Required.

tasks.title: Apply and verify the battery EPR registration-number marking
tasks.user_goal: Ensure every in-scope battery or battery pack in the imported equipment carries the producer's current EPR registration number through a legally permitted marking method before sale.
tasks.trigger: The importer is a producer of a battery or equipment containing a battery and has received the CPCB EPR registration number; the 31 March 2025 marking date has passed.

timelines.label: Battery EPR registration-number marking date
timelines.applicability: Schedule I paragraph 2(ia); by the verification date the date has passed, so in-scope demo stock must comply before sale.

steps: Retrieve the exact active producer EPR registration number from the CPCB certificate/portal and bind it to the importer and battery-equipped SKU.
Ensure the battery or battery pack is appropriately marked with that registration number under Schedule I paragraph 2(ia).

If using the 2025 alternative, first provide the required information in writing to CPCB, then print a barcode or QR code containing the number on the battery/battery pack, the equipment containing it, either packaging, or eligible bulk packaging; alternatively print the EPR registration number on the product information brochure.
Inspect a physical sale-unit/package/brochure from the actual lot, scan any barcode/QR code and reconcile the displayed number to the active CPCB registration.
Retain the controlled artwork, lot sample/capture and CPCB written-information/portal evidence where the alternative method is used.
tasks.tracking: Track marking method, registration number, artwork version, CPCB notice, SKU and lot; revalidate after any registration, product, packaging or brochure change.
tasks.rejection_handling: Quarantine unmarked, unreadable, wrong-number or wrong-producer stock; correct only through a legally validated marking/rework route before sale.
tasks.escalation: Ask CPCB in writing when the selected placement or alternative notification route is uncertain; do not treat a registration certificate alone as marking approval.

state_local_dependency.description: The battery EPR marking obligation is Central; separate package or local controls may coexist.

tasks.fail_closed_note: CPCB registration, draft artwork or supplier assurance is not proof that the actual sale lot bears the correct registration-number marking.

tasks.title: Register as an e-waste producer when the exact equipment is in Schedule I
tasks.user_goal: Place covered electrical or electronic equipment on the Indian market only under the producer's own current CPCB e-waste registration.
tasks.trigger: The exact product is established to be electrical/electronic equipment listed in Schedule I of the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022.

fees_duties.label: E-waste producer registration charge
fees_duties.applicability: Use the current authenticated CPCB portal demand for the actual role/category; no universal current amount is admitted.

steps: Record the exact Schedule-I category and code with the model facts; keep the branch unresolved if the mapping is not supportable.
Apply as the producer through CPCB's E-Waste EPR Portal using the importer's own entity and category data.
Retain the granted registration certificate and match entity, producer role, covered category/status and validity before placing the product on the market.
Build the applicable target, certificate, return and RoHS evidence controls from the current rules and actual portal registration.
tasks.tracking: Track CPCB registration/status, category, targets, EPR certificates and filings by financial year.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct entity/category/quantity objections in the CPCB case and quarantine market placement until registration is granted and matched.
tasks.escalation: Seek written CPCB category/portal clarification when Schedule-I mapping or a portal objection remains unresolved.

state_local_dependency.description: Central producer registration is separate from any facility/recycler permission administered by a State Pollution Control Board.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The public route is verified, but the demo headphones remain outside this task until exact Schedule-I mapping is proven.

tasks.title: Register and operate the plastic-packaging PIBO branch when applicable
tasks.user_goal: Place products in regulated plastic packaging on the Indian market only under the correct importer/producer/brand-owner registration and EPR controls.
tasks.trigger: The importer is a producer, importer or brand owner placing plastic packaging covered by Schedule II of the Plastic Waste Management Rules on the Indian market.

fees_duties.label: Plastic EPR registration/application charge
fees_duties.applicability: Role, category and live Common EPR Portal determine the amount; no universal current amount is admitted.

steps: Complete a packaging BOM and determine the importer's PIBO role and each applicable plastic-packaging category under the current rules.
Register through CPCB's centralised online route, now accessed through the Common EPR Portal after the 28 June 2026 migration.
Retain the granted role/category registration and reconcile packaging quantities, EPR certificates, targets and returns for the applicable period.
Do not treat a packaging vendor or recycler agreement as the importer's registration or as proof of completed targets.
tasks.tracking: Track Common EPR Portal status, category, quantity, certificates, targets and returns against purchasing/import records.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct PIBO role/category/entity evidence through the CPCB case and hold affected market placement while registration is absent.
tasks.escalation: Use CPCB's waste-stream help/grievance route for a Common EPR identity migration or role/category issue and preserve the ticket.

state_local_dependency.description: Central PIBO registration does not establish State permissions for waste-processing facilities or other local premises obligations.

tasks.fail_closed_note: The legal role and current portal route are established, but actual packaging composition, quantities and authenticated filing state remain shipment/user evidence.

tasks.title: Complete Legal Metrology registration and release retail label artwork
tasks.user_goal: Import and offer a pre-packaged commodity only with the current importer registration and mandatory declarations that apply to its package/channel.
tasks.trigger: The goods are imported/sold as a pre-packaged commodity within the current Legal Metrology rules.

fees_duties.label: Rule 27 registration/other Legal Metrology fee
fees_duties.applicability: Exact current jurisdiction, application and fee were not fully verified from public portal text.

timelines.label: Registration timing
timelines.applicability: Do not rely on older FAQ timing without checking current rules and the competent jurisdiction.

steps: Confirm package and transaction coverage, exemptions, importer/packer identity and competent Central/State jurisdiction under the current rules.

For Rule 27 Packaged Commodities Registration, follow the Department portal's current instruction to apply through NSWS; retain the granted reference/certificate and verify it in the public certificate registry where listed.

Validate artwork for manufacturer/packer/importer identity and address, country of origin for imported goods, common/generic name, net quantity, month/year where required, MRP inclusive of taxes, consumer-care details and every product-specific declaration.
Inspect physical samples and online listing fields before customs clearance/sale; quarantine mismatched stock.
tasks.tracking: Track the NSWS application/reference and retain the granted certificate, public certificate-registry result, released artwork, package samples, change log and channel listing capture.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct the registration/label through the competent authority; do not cover noncompliance with an uncontrolled sticker without legal validation.
tasks.escalation: Use the Department portal's published dirwm-ca@nic.in contact and confirm central versus State Controller jurisdiction/current amendments before printing or relabelling.

state_local_dependency.description: Legal Metrology administration/enforcement may depend on importer premises and State/UT jurisdiction; exact local procedure is intentionally unresolved.

tasks.fail_closed_note: DGFT's summary of declarations is a baseline, not a complete product/channel-specific artwork approval.

tasks.title: Obtain other sector regulator permits and prepare PGA clearance
tasks.user_goal: Route food, health, plant, animal, wildlife, hazardous and other specially regulated goods through the competent authority before and at import.
tasks.trigger: A product trait, tariff condition or risk-management referral invokes another Central product regulator/PGA.

fees_duties.label: Sector licence/testing/inspection fee
fees_duties.applicability: Competent regulator, product, quantity, port and service determine the fee.

steps: Identify the operative statute/notification, regulated category, importer eligibility, pre-import permit/licence and designated port for the exact goods.
Obtain the pre-import permission before dispatch where required and prepare product-specific certificates/test reports.
For referred Bills of Entry, use the current SWIFT/PGA route, upload additional documents, answer queries, schedule inspection/sampling and obtain NOC or release decision.
Confirm local port rollout before assuming a standalone PGA portal is replaced; Plant Quarantine migration is phased.
tasks.tracking: Track both the regulator licence/permit and shipment-level NOC/inspection status; they are distinct proofs.
tasks.rejection_handling: Do not divert to an unapproved port or sell rejected goods; follow regulator-directed treatment, re-export, destruction, appeal or correction.
tasks.escalation: Use the competent PGA's escalation and ICEGATE Helpdesk with the Bill of Entry/referral reference; resolve phased-route ambiguity before filing.

state_local_dependency.description: Some goods also require State drug, food, excise, pollution or premises licences; exact procedure depends on product and location.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Customs filing does not replace a pre-import sector permit; a licence does not replace shipment-level NOC where required.

tasks.title: Establish GST registration and import-credit readiness
tasks.user_goal: Use the correct GST identity and preserve only supportable import IGST credit and sale invoicing.
tasks.trigger: Before filing with a GSTIN, claiming import IGST credit or making taxable supplies.
steps: Determine registration liability and State/UT principal/additional places from the actual supply, turnover, marketplace and location facts; a liable person applies in each relevant State/UT within the section 25 timing using the actual date liability arose.
If required, apply on GST Portal under Services > Registration > New Registration and complete the current Aadhaar/biometric/risk-based process shown for the case.
Download the registration certificate and ensure GSTIN/entity/address align with DGFT/ICEGATE records used for the import.
For import IGST credit, retain the Bill of Entry/customs document and satisfy the statutory possession/receipt/tax-paid/return conditions before claim.
Before a taxable-goods sale by a registered person, configure the tax invoice so it is issued before or at removal/delivery and contains the current rule 46 particulars.
tasks.tracking: Track ARN/clarifications/certificate on GST Portal and reconcile customs import data to books and returns.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use GST Portal's clarification route for notices; correct authoritative entity/address evidence rather than creating inconsistent registrations.
tasks.escalation: Escalate multi-State, marketplace, place-of-supply or credit uncertainty to a qualified GST practitioner and the jurisdictional officer as appropriate.

state_local_dependency.description: GST registration is administered by Central/State tax authorities and depends on the State/UT place of business and supply facts.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Being an importer does not by itself establish the unverified GST registration/rate/invoice conclusions for every business model.

tasks.title: Appoint and control necessary logistics and regulated private actors
tasks.user_goal: Ensure carrier, freight forwarder, customs broker, custodian, bank and laboratory roles are authorised, scoped and evidenced without outsourcing legal responsibility.
tasks.trigger: Before booking transport, testing, customs filing or payment.

fees_duties.label: Private logistics, brokerage, laboratory, custody and bank charges
fees_duties.applicability: Commercial quotes and service facts are outside official-source verification.

steps: Verify the current authority/accreditation and exact service scope of each regulated actor used.
Issue written authority and data-sharing boundaries to the customs broker and other agents; preserve importer review of declarations.
Book only after policy and regulator dispatch gates are satisfied and route/port conditions are confirmed.
Require shipment, test, custody and payment artifacts tied to the same product/shipment identifiers.
tasks.tracking: Maintain authority letters, licences/accreditations, quotes, milestones and exceptions by actor and shipment.
tasks.rejection_handling: Replace or rescope an actor whose authority, accreditation or data does not match the task; correct filing errors through customs records.
tasks.escalation: Escalate fraud, document substitution or custody loss to the competent regulator/customs/bank and preserve evidence.

state_local_dependency.description: Actor regulation can involve local offices, but no State procedure is needed to define this control task.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A broker's acceptance or carrier booking does not prove import permission, classification or regulatory compliance.

tasks.title: Prepare and upload the customs document set
tasks.user_goal: Create a consistent, retrievable set of commercial, transport and regulatory documents for electronic customs filing.
tasks.trigger: Applicable pre-import permissions exist and final shipping documents are available.
steps: Reconcile commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, quantities, values, marks, model and party identities.
Upload the Bill of Lading/Air Waybill, commercial invoice, packing list or invoice-cum-packing list and every commodity/PGA supporting document through eSanchit as applicable.
Record each document reference and map it to the correct Bill of Entry line and declaration.
Run a pre-filing check against authorisation/licence quantity, value, port, validity and model scope.
tasks.tracking: Track eSanchit document references and version/hash in the shipment file; never overwrite the signed source without audit trail.
tasks.rejection_handling: Correct inconsistent or illegible documents and re-upload under the controlled customs process; do not fabricate missing certificates.
tasks.escalation: Use ICEGATE Helpdesk/Customs Service Centre when electronic upload is unavailable, preserving the error and document reference.

state_local_dependency.description: The customs document channel is central; source documents may evidence separate State permissions.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Upload success proves document transmission, not acceptance, accuracy, NOC or customs release.

tasks.title: File the Integrated Bill of Entry and monitor assessment
tasks.user_goal: Make the import declaration electronically with supportable classification, value, origin, permits and self-assessment.
tasks.trigger: Shipment and arrival data satisfy the current statutory filing window and all pre-import blockers are closed.

timelines.label: Statutory Bill of Entry filing deadline
timelines.applicability: Section 46 contains timing rules and exceptions; exact current deadline for the route/date was not restated in this pack and must be checked before arrival.

steps: Review every line, declaration, notification claim, valuation element, origin, licence/PGA reference and document reference before filing.
Submit the Bill of Entry electronically on the customs automated system through ICEGATE or an authorised customs broker.
Capture the Bill of Entry number/date and monitor the logged-in Job Status dashboard; preserve the positive or negative acknowledgement and processed-BE message.
Do not treat 'BE No Generated' or 'Ready for Duty Payment' as release.
tasks.tracking: Use ICEGATE Bill of Entry Job Status and preserve status-detail exports and query history.
tasks.rejection_handling: A negative acknowledgement is not a filed Bill of Entry: correct the stated validation error and resubmit. After acceptance, correct errors only through the lawful amendment/reassessment process and answer query messages with sourced evidence.
tasks.escalation: Use the 24x7 ICEGATE Helpdesk (1800-3010-1000 or icegatehelpdesk@icegate.gov.in) or assessing group with BE/message reference and error/status evidence; use Customs Service Centre only where access is unavailable.

state_local_dependency.description: Bill of Entry filing is central customs procedure.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A filed declaration is not proof that the goods are admissible, correctly classified, duty-paid or released.

tasks.title: Answer customs/PGA queries and complete inspection, sampling or testing
tasks.user_goal: Resolve assessment and product-agency referrals with shipment-specific evidence while preserving the audit trail.
tasks.trigger: ICEGATE/customs/PGA status shows a query, document request, examination, inspection, sampling, testing or NOC requirement.

fees_duties.label: Testing, handling, storage/demurrage or treatment charges
fees_duties.applicability: Only assessed/private invoices and the applicable regulator rules can establish amounts.

steps: Read the exact query/status and preserve it before responding.
Submit responsive model/shipment evidence using the current query-reply message/service through ICEGATE/SWIFT and arrange examination/sampling with authorised actors.
Track separate customs assessment and PGA NOC decisions; download the NOC/rejection artifact where the dashboard provides it.
If noncompliance is found, quarantine goods and follow the written remediation/re-export/destruction direction.
tasks.tracking: Use ICEGATE job-status details, SWIFT query/inspection status and regulator references; record time and respondent for every submission.
tasks.rejection_handling: Do not make unsupported declarations; correct, test, re-export, destroy or appeal only under the written customs/regulator route.
tasks.escalation: Escalate stalled/mismatched referrals to ICEGATE Helpdesk and the competent customs/PGA office with the BE reference and status export.

state_local_dependency.description: Border inspection is central/PGA; destination controls remain separate.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Silence, elapsed time or a customs status does not equal a regulator NOC.

tasks.title: Pay the assessed amount and obtain Customs Out of Charge
tasks.user_goal: Pay only the assessment tied to the Bill of Entry and take delivery only after formal customs release.
tasks.trigger: ICEGATE shows the assessed Bill of Entry ready for duty payment and all required NOCs/examination conditions are satisfied.

fees_duties.label: Customs assessment payable
fees_duties.applicability: Use only the live assessment/challan for this Bill of Entry; this pack supplies no number.

steps: Reconcile the assessment/challan to the Bill of Entry, legal calculation and approval from the importer.
Pay through the current ICEGATE customs payment service using the importer-authorised bank/payment channel.
Retain the payment confirmation and wait for formal Out of Charge status/order.
Reconcile custodian/carrier release and take delivery without treating it as sale readiness.
tasks.tracking: Track Ready for Duty Payment, payment acknowledgement, OOC Issuance and final customs/custodian release references.
tasks.rejection_handling: Resolve failed/duplicate payment only through ICEGATE/bank reconciliation; do not pay to an unverified account or agent demand.
tasks.escalation: Escalate status/payment mismatch to ICEGATE Helpdesk, bank and assessing customs office with BE/challan/reference evidence.

state_local_dependency.description: Customs payment and OOC are central; taking goods to a premises may require State/local compliance.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Payment or physical possession without Out of Charge is not lawful customs release; OOC is not a product-sale approval.

tasks.title: Resolve genuine State/UT and local dependencies
tasks.user_goal: Confirm the permissions tied to the actual place of business, storage, retail channel and product without inventing a generic state procedure.
tasks.trigger: The importer knows the State/UT, premises, storage, employees, product and sales channels.
steps: Identify actual State/UT and municipal jurisdiction for registered office, warehouse, shop, online operations and any regulated facility.
Ask the competent authorities whether trade/shop, fire, premises, professional-tax, state pollution, Legal Metrology, sector retail/storage or state-excise permissions apply.
For alcohol or another State-controlled commodity, verify the specific State requirements before selecting the import/sale path.
Record each not-applicable conclusion or granted permission with the authority, version/date and premises/product scope.
tasks.tracking: Maintain a location-by-location register with renewals and changes; do not copy conclusions between States or premises.
tasks.rejection_handling: Do not operate from or sell at the affected premises until the competent State/local authority resolves the gap.
tasks.escalation: Use the named State/UT/municipal department and local counsel; no nationwide portal or timeline is asserted here.

state_local_dependency.description: This task is entirely location- and product-dependent; central sources only establish that such dependencies can coexist.

tasks.fail_closed_note: A central registration or customs OOC does not waive State/UT or municipal requirements.

tasks.title: Run the final sale-release gate
tasks.user_goal: Release only stock whose customs, product, tax, label, environmental and location proofs all match the actual model and lot.
tasks.trigger: Customs OOC and physical receipt exist, before advertising, offering, invoicing, distributing or selling the first unit.
steps: Match received model, lot, quantity, markings, packaging and accessories to invoice, Bill of Entry and approval scope.

Verify OOC, applicable BIS/ETA/REPA/MTCTE/sector certificates or exact exceptions, waste-stream registrations, the physical battery EPR registration-number marking proof, Legal Metrology registration/declarations, GST identity/invoice control and State/local matrix.
Inspect physical labels and online listing content; quarantine discrepant units.
Authorise sale in writing and configure invoice/return/EPR/complaint/recall records; schedule ongoing compliance reviews.
tasks.tracking: Use lot-level release status and retain linked proofs through sale, return, regulator audit and EPR/recall lifecycle.
tasks.rejection_handling: Keep stock quarantined; correct labels/registrations only through lawful routes, or re-export/destroy/recall as directed.
tasks.escalation: Escalate any certificate/lot mismatch, suspension, recall or regulator notice to the compliance owner and competent authority immediately.

state_local_dependency.description: Sale release remains blocked until the actual State/UT/local dependency matrix is closed.

tasks.fail_closed_note: Customs release is necessary but never sufficient proof that a regulated product may be sold.

tasks.title: Operate periodic, incident and rejection compliance
tasks.user_goal: Keep licences, returns, EPR, GST, records, complaints and corrective actions current after first sale.
tasks.trigger: After registration/import/sale, on each statutory period, change, complaint, nonconformity, expiry, suspension, recall or authority notice.
steps: Build a compliance calendar from each actual licence, registration, return, target and condition; do not use a generic frequency.
Reconcile GST/customs records, EPR quantities/certificates, complaints, warranty returns and regulator portal status.
Before any model, factory, brand, radio, package, premises or supplier change, rerun scope and approval checks.
Quarantine/recall affected stock, notify authorities and remediate/re-export/destroy when required by an incident or rejection.
tasks.tracking: Maintain dated returns, acknowledgements, renewals, target reconciliation, incident log and regulator correspondence.
tasks.rejection_handling: Use each authority's notice/clarification/appeal route; never cure a missed filing by backdating evidence.
tasks.escalation: Escalate safety, counterfeit-document, environmental, tax or product nonconformity incidents promptly to the competent authority and counsel.

state_local_dependency.description: State/local renewals, returns and incident reporting depend on the permissions identified in task imp.t20.

tasks.fail_closed_note: This pack does not invent universal filing dates; derive the calendar from the live obligation and granted instrument.

dependency_edges.condition: The actual Indian importer entity is identified.
ICEGATE registration/mapping uses the importer IEC identity.
Classification requires model-level objective facts.
Duty/origin analysis requires a supported tariff classification.
Applies only when current DGFT policy/condition requires authorisation.
Regulator mapping requires product traits and intended use.
Tariff/policy analysis informs but does not alone determine product-regulator scope.
Applies when a BIS QCO/compulsory scheme covers the exact product.
Applies when the product contains radio equipment.
Applies when current MTCTE scope covers or may cover the product.
Applies when a battery, Schedule-I EEE, plastic packaging or another EPR stream is present.
Applies when the goods are regulated pre-packaged commodities.
Applies when a sector trait or customs risk referral invokes a PGA.
Importer identity and location/supply facts are known.
The importer can authorise and supervise electronic customs work.
Do not book dispatch until regulator/port blockers are identified and closed.
A required DGFT authorisation must be granted before filing/dispatch.
Applicable BIS proof must match the shipment.
Applicable WPC/spectrum authorisation must be obtained.
Applicable MTCTE certificate must be obtained.
Applicable pre-business EPR registration must be in force.
Required Legal Metrology registration/label evidence must be ready.
Any pre-import sector permit must be granted.
Final carrier/commercial documents and controlled filing authority exist.
The controlled supporting-document set is complete.
Assessment, query, examination or PGA referral occurs.
A shipment-specific assessment/challan exists.
Unresolved customs queries, inspections or required NOCs block OOC.
Central review identifies which product/location questions must be asked locally.
GST State/UT and place-of-business facts inform the local matrix.
Customs OOC and physical receipt are necessary but not sufficient for sale.
Unresolved applicable State/local permissions block sale.
BIS proof is a sale gate when applicable.
WPC/spectrum proof is a sale gate when applicable.
MTCTE proof is a sale gate when applicable.
EPR/producer proof is a sale gate when applicable.
Legal Metrology proof and physical/online declarations are sale gates when applicable.
Sector licence/NOC is a sale gate when applicable.
Correct GST identity/invoicing treatment must be established before taxable sale.
First sale begins periodic, complaint, change-control and incident obligations.
For a battery or equipment containing a battery, the active CPCB producer registration number is required before the number can be marked and verified.
When battery EPR applies, the actual sale lot cannot be released until the correct registration-number marking and any required CPCB written-information record are verified.
Use the CAAR route when material classification ambiguity remains and an advance ruling is sought.
Where the pending classification question changes admissibility, authorisation or regulator scope, do not dispatch/file until the ruling or another supportable resolution closes it.
A final in-scope advance ruling controls the working classification used in the shipment duty analysis.
A BIS suspension, cancellation, expiry, notice or scope mismatch triggers the remediation hold.
Affected goods cannot be dispatched/filed as covered until current BIS scope is restored or otherwise lawfully resolved.
Affected goods cannot be released for sale on a suspended, cancelled, expired or mismatched BIS record.
Apply REPA rule 4 and rule 10 to every proposed import/possession-for-sale activity involving radio equipment.
Where REPA applies, a grant matching the activity/equipment is required before dispatch/filing; otherwise retain exact rule 10 exception proof.
Sale is blocked until REPA coverage or an exception that permits the intended commercial activity is evidenced.
Apply when the exact product is established within E-Waste Rules Schedule I.
Covered EEE cannot be released for sale without the producer's matching active e-waste registration.
Apply when the importer's actual packaging and PIBO role fall within plastic-packaging EPR.
Covered plastic-packaging market placement is blocked until the matching PIBO registration and required current-period controls exist.

authorities_actors.name: Indian importer of record / producer / seller
authorities_actors.role: Owns facts, declarations, applications, payments, product release and continuing compliance.
authorities_actors.jurisdiction: India and the importer's actual State/UT locations

authorities_actors.name: Directorate General of Foreign Trade
authorities_actors.role: Issues IEC and administers ITC(HS) import policy and restricted import authorisations.
authorities_actors.channel: DGFT website and Import Management System

authorities_actors.name: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs / jurisdictional Customs
authorities_actors.role: Administers customs declaration, assessment, examination, duty and release.
authorities_actors.jurisdiction: India customs territory and port/airport/ICD jurisdiction
authorities_actors.channel: Customs automated system, ICEGATE and customs offices

authorities_actors.name: ICEGATE
authorities_actors.role: National electronic gateway for registration, documents, Bill of Entry status, payment-facing services and SWIFT.

authorities_actors.name: Bureau of Indian Standards
authorities_actors.role: Administers compulsory product certification/registration and public licence checks.

authorities_actors.name: Department of Telecommunications / Wireless Planning and Coordination Wing
authorities_actors.role: Administers spectrum and wireless equipment authorisations.
authorities_actors.channel: DoT eServices and current authorisation portal

authorities_actors.name: Telecommunication Engineering Centre
authorities_actors.role: Administers MTCTE conformity assessment for notified telecom equipment.

authorities_actors.name: Central Pollution Control Board
authorities_actors.role: Administers central EPR portals/registrations and receives the written information used for the battery-marking alternative.
authorities_actors.channel: CPCB EPR portals and written-information route

authorities_actors.name: Department of Consumer Affairs / Legal Metrology
authorities_actors.role: Administers packaged-commodity requirements and central portal routes, alongside competent State authorities.
authorities_actors.channel: Legal Metrology portal and competent Controller/Director

authorities_actors.name: GST Portal / Central and State tax administration
authorities_actors.role: Registration, certificate, clarification and GST return/credit framework.
authorities_actors.jurisdiction: India and relevant State/UT GST jurisdiction

authorities_actors.name: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
authorities_actors.role: Regulates imported food and issues shipment NOC/rejection through current SWIFT flow where applicable.
authorities_actors.jurisdiction: India and notified points of entry
authorities_actors.channel: ICEGATE SWIFT Unified Dashboard and FSSAI systems

authorities_actors.name: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation
authorities_actors.role: Regulates import of drugs, cosmetics and medical devices within its scope and shipment referrals.
authorities_actors.jurisdiction: India and notified points of entry

authorities_actors.name: Plant Quarantine, Animal Quarantine and wildlife authorities
authorities_actors.role: Administer permits, inspection and NOC for covered plant, animal and wildlife consignments.
authorities_actors.jurisdiction: India and designated points of entry
authorities_actors.channel: Competent authority systems and phased ICEGATE SWIFT routes

authorities_actors.name: Other competent Central product regulator
authorities_actors.role: Covers product-specific regimes such as hazardous chemicals, pesticides, petroleum/explosives, ODS, energy labelling or another notified control after fact-specific identification.
authorities_actors.channel: Exact authority/portal must be established from the operative notification

authorities_actors.name: Competent State/UT and municipal authorities

authorities_actors.channel: Not universal; identify after location/product facts

authorities_actors.name: Licensed customs broker
authorities_actors.role: May prepare/file customs data under authority while the importer retains responsibility for facts and review.

authorities_actors.name: Carrier / freight forwarder
authorities_actors.role: Transports goods and supplies transport/arrival documents and milestones.

authorities_actors.name: Port/airport/ICD custodian
authorities_actors.role: Holds and releases cargo under customs/port control.

authorities_actors.name: Authorised bank/payment channel
authorities_actors.role: Supports entity banking, trade payment and customs payment reconciliation.

authorities_actors.name: Recognised/accredited test laboratory
authorities_actors.role: Produces model-specific test evidence only within its current recognition/accreditation scope.

authorities_actors.name: Registered recycler/refurbisher and EPR counterparties

authorities_actors.channel: CPCB EPR portals and controlled contracts

authorities_actors.name: Foreign manufacturer / factory

portal_journeys.name: DGFT Apply/Update IEC
portal_journeys.authentication: DGFT account and current identity/authentication controls for the actual entity.
portal_journeys.navigation: DGFT website > Apply for IEC or Update IEC; the official ANF-2A states the process is electronic and paperless.

portal_journeys.submission_proof: Portal reference plus downloaded e-IEC certificate.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: DGFT account/application history and View your IEC verification facility.
portal_journeys.exception_route: DGFT grievance/help channel using the application reference.
portal_journeys.access_limitation: Authenticated form, fee and case-specific validation were not accessible without an applicant account.

portal_journeys.name: DGFT Import Authorisation for Restricted Imports
portal_journeys.authentication: DGFT entity login and current signing/authentication control.
portal_journeys.navigation: Services > Import Management System > Import Authorization for Restricted Imports > Apply for New Authorization.
inputs_uploads: Country, ITC(HS), description/specifications, quantity/UOM and CIF values
Port, purpose, detailed justification and sector documents
portal_journeys.submission_proof: Application reference; only the granted authorisation is completion proof.
portal_journeys.tracking_route: DGFT application history and authorisation record.
portal_journeys.exception_route: DGFT deficiency/grievance/review route shown for the case.
