claims.subject: Cross-cutting domestic compliance
claims.applicability: All imported goods
claims.locator: General Notes to Import Policy 2025, PDF p.1, General Note 1, opening paragraph.

claims.statement: A person/entity intending to import or export requires IEC, subject to the exemptions in HBP paragraph 2.07.
claims.subject: IEC eligibility
claims.applicability: Commercial importer unless a verified exemption applies
claims.locator: ANF-2A dated 19-01-2026, PDF p.7, note under Part I: 'All persons/entities who intend to import/export are required to have an IEC', with HBP 2.07 exception.

claims.statement: The DGFT IEC application/update process is electronic and paperless and collects entity/PAN/contact/constitution/bank and related particulars.
claims.subject: IEC application route and inputs
claims.applicability: IEC application or update
claims.locator: ANF-2A dated 19-01-2026, PDF pp.1-3 and p.7; header states Apply for IEC/Update IEC and no hard/scanned copies, Parts A-C list entity, PAN, address, contact, constitution and bank fields.

claims.statement: DGFT's e-IEC certificate instructs users to verify authenticity through the DGFT 'View your IEC' facility.
claims.subject: IEC completion proof
claims.applicability: Granted e-IEC
claims.locator: ANF-2A dated 19-01-2026, PDF p.9, sample e-IEC certificate note on verification through DGFT website > View your IEC.

claims.statement: ICEGATE currently lists Registration on ICEGATE, Matching IEC GSTIN and Register/Update DSC services; its official FAQ describes a paperless registration flow based on DGFT/GSTN-matching identity/contact data.
claims.subject: ICEGATE registration
claims.applicability: Importer/customs electronic user
claims.locator: ICEGATE Registration service page, current listings dated 05-06-2025/21-11-2024/22-12-2025; Registration FAQ, FAQs 5-9.

claims.statement: The importer must enter a Bill of Entry electronically on the customs automated system for home consumption or warehousing; an officer may permit another manner only where electronic entry is not feasible.
claims.subject: Bill of Entry filing
claims.applicability: Imported goods entered for home consumption or warehousing
claims.locator: Customs Act, 1962, Section 46(1), current CBIC Tax Information Portal text.

claims.statement: The importer self-assesses duty, while the proper officer may verify the entries and require examination, testing, documents or information.
claims.subject: Customs assessment
claims.applicability: Bill of Entry assessment
claims.locator: Customs Act, 1962, Section 17(1)-(3), current CBIC Tax Information Portal text.

claims.statement: Customs may verify self-assessment and require documents/information and examination or testing of imported goods.
claims.subject: Customs verification
claims.applicability: Where the proper officer selects or requires verification
claims.locator: Customs Act, 1962, Section 17(2)-(3), current CBIC Tax Information Portal text.

claims.statement: Customs value is generally transaction value for goods sold for export to India where buyer and seller are unrelated and price is the sole consideration, with specified cost/service additions under the valuation rules; other cases are determined under the rules.
claims.subject: Customs valuation framework
claims.applicability: Imported goods valuation
claims.locator: Customs Act, 1962, Section 14(1), including provisos and transaction-value definition on CBIC Tax Information Portal.

claims.statement: Imported articles are additionally liable to integrated tax under Customs Tariff Act Section 3, calculated on the statutory import-tax value; this claim does not establish a product-specific rate or amount.
claims.subject: Import IGST legal basis
claims.applicability: Taxable imported articles
claims.locator: Customs Tariff Act, 1975, Section 3(7)-(8), current CBIC Tax Information Portal text.

claims.statement: ICEGATE presents its Customs Compliance Information Portal as an aid for customs procedures, compliance information and tariff/duty discovery, but it is not admitted here as binding classification or assessment proof.
claims.subject: Customs information/calculation aid
claims.applicability: Pre-filing research and calculation
claims.locator: ICEGATE Services page description of Customs Compliance Information Portal, live 28-08-2026.

claims.statement: The Customs Authority for Advance Rulings Regulations route a Form CAAR-1 application to the jurisdictional Authority determined by the applicant's address, providing an official pre-transaction path for a material customs question.
claims.subject: Customs advance-ruling acquisition route
claims.applicability: Applicant with a proposed customs transaction/question; the ruling binds only within its legal and factual scope
claims.locator: Customs Authority for Advance Rulings Regulations, 2021 as amended, regulation 6; official Form CAAR-1 pages 1-8.

claims.statement: DGFT's restricted-import application route is fully electronic and asks for country, ITC(HS), description/specifications, quantity/UOM, CIF value, port, purpose and detailed justification plus applicable sector documents.
claims.subject: Restricted import authorisation
claims.applicability: Goods whose current policy requires DGFT import authorisation
claims.locator: ANF-2M, PDF pp.1-3; heading/navigation statement and Parts A-C/application detail fields.

claims.statement: The customs supporting-document set includes Bill of Lading/Air Waybill, commercial invoice and packing list or invoice-cum-packing list, with additional documents depending on commodity, notification and PGA requirements.
claims.subject: eSanchit import documents
claims.applicability: Electronic import declaration; extra documents are conditional
claims.locator: ICEGATE eSANCHIT Process Guide, section 1.9 'Mandatory documents for import/export', current official file path dated 2025-09.

claims.statement: ICEGATE's logged-in Bill of Entry Job Status displays assessment/payment/examination/query/PGA/OOC stages and permits detailed status export.
claims.subject: Bill of Entry tracking
claims.applicability: Filed Bill of Entry
claims.locator: Advisory for Checking Bill of Entry Status on ICEGATE 2.0 dated 12-01-2026, dashboard/navigation and status list.

claims.statement: ICEGATE's current e-filing message catalogue distinguishes Bill-of-Entry positive acknowledgement, negative acknowledgement, processed Bill of Entry, query and query-reply messages; a negative acknowledgement must therefore be corrected and resubmitted rather than treated as a filed entry, while accepted query cases use the query-reply route.
claims.subject: Bill of Entry rejection and query remediation
claims.applicability: Electronic Bill of Entry submission and subsequent customs query
claims.locator: ICEGATE E-filing Messages page, Bill of Entry message list including positive acknowledgement, negative acknowledgement, processed BE, query and query reply; Services page current helpdesk details.

claims.statement: ICEGATE SWIFT provides a single-window route; 2026 advisories moved referred FSSAI and CDSCO Bills of Entry to the SWIFT Unified Dashboard for documents, queries, inspection and NOC/rejection handling.
claims.subject: PGA single-window clearance
claims.applicability: Bills of Entry referred to an integrated PGA
claims.locator: ICEGATE Single Window service page; FSSAI advisory dated 02-02-2026; CDSCO advisory dated 22-01-2026, each describing dashboard fields/documents/status/query/inspection/NOC download.

claims.statement: Plant Quarantine's SWIFT/PQMS transition is phased by location/readiness, so the exact filing route cannot be selected without the intended port and current rollout confirmation.
claims.subject: Plant Quarantine portal route
claims.applicability: Covered plant/plant-product consignments
claims.locator: Updated Advisory PQMS 4.7 dated 15-04-2026, phased/pilot rollout and statement that separate PQMS filing is not required only for covered implementation.

claims.statement: Customs Service Centres provide data-entry and document/status facilities where trade cannot file from its premises; this is an access fallback, not substantive approval.
claims.subject: Customs offline-assisted access
claims.applicability: Verified inability to use normal electronic filing from premises
claims.locator: ICEGATE Customs Service Centres page, services list including Bill of Entry data entry/checklist/query/challan/OOC printing/status, live 28-08-2026.

claims.statement: Customs may order clearance for home consumption only when the goods are not prohibited and assessed duty/charges are paid; the Out of Charge decision does not itself prove post-import sale compliance.
claims.subject: Customs home-consumption release
claims.applicability: Bill of Entry for home consumption
claims.locator: Customs Act, 1962, Section 47(1), current CBIC Tax Information Portal text; second sentence is the pack's conservative inference from separate domestic-law gates.

claims.statement: Products covered by a notified BIS compulsory-certification/QCO regime must meet the applicable standard and bear/use the Standard Mark only under the required BIS licence/registration/CoC.
claims.subject: BIS compulsory certification
claims.applicability: Exact product listed in a current QCO/compulsory scheme
claims.locator: BIS Products under Compulsory Certification page, Scheme/QCO explanation, last updated 15-04-2026.

claims.statement: BIS's current Scheme-II list includes 'Wireless Headphone and Earphone' against IS/IEC 62368 (Part 1):2023.
claims.subject: BIS CRS product list
claims.applicability: Products objectively within that category; exact model/factory coverage still requires verification
claims.locator: BIS Scheme-II Registration Scheme list, item 51, 'Wireless Headphone and Earphone', IS/IEC 62368 (Part 1):2023; page accessed 28-08-2026.

claims.statement: The substituted 2026 Scheme II requires a manufacturer to identify the applicable standard/essential requirements, manufacturing/testing capability, model and brand; apply separately for each product in Form I and generally each brand; submit Form II, a third-party laboratory report, the applicable Form III affidavit and, for a foreign manufacturer, Form IV; BIS issues the granted licence in Form V with its scope.
claims.subject: BIS Scheme-II application and grant sequence
claims.applicability: New Scheme-II applicant manufacturer after the 2026 amendment took effect
claims.locator: BIS (Conformity Assessment) Amendment Regulations, 2026, Schedule-II substituted Scheme II, paragraph 3(1)-(5), Gazette English PDF pp.41-42; Forms I-V at PDF pp.49-61.

claims.statement: Under substituted Scheme II, the application fee, annual licence fee and renewal application fee are INR 1,000 each; yearly advance processing is INR 25,000 per application; each additional test report is INR 20,000; and inclusion of new varieties/models or scope extension is INR 30,000 per application.
claims.subject: BIS Scheme-II statutory fees
claims.applicability: Only the stated Scheme-II transaction; statutory concessions and other testing/service costs require separate case treatment
claims.locator: BIS (Conformity Assessment) Amendment Regulations, 2026, substituted Scheme II paragraph 5(1)-(3) and 5(7), Gazette English PDF p.43.

claims.statement: A Scheme-II licence is granted initially for up to five years and may be renewed for a further period up to five years, with required fee paid annually in advance.
claims.subject: BIS Scheme-II licence validity
claims.applicability: A granted Scheme-II licence; actual dates are those in the Form V licence
claims.locator: BIS (Conformity Assessment) Amendment Regulations, 2026, substituted Scheme II paragraph 8(1)-(3), Gazette English PDF p.44.

claims.statement: BIS CRS provides a public registered-manufacturer search with registration, model/product, status, validity and brand fields that can be used to validate claimed coverage.
claims.subject: BIS CRS public verification
claims.applicability: Claimed CRS registration/model coverage
claims.locator: BIS CRS Registered Manufacturers search page and displayed search/result fields, accessed 28-08-2026.

claims.statement: Current Scheme II requires at least 21 days' notice before suspension or cancellation; after cancellation the licensee must stop using the Standard Mark and stop supplying, importing, distributing or selling goods under the cancelled licence. BIS publishes CRS support and a DDG (Registration) grievance channel.
claims.subject: BIS suspension/cancellation remedy
claims.applicability: Scheme-II licence under notice, suspension or cancellation
claims.locator: BIS (Conformity Assessment) Amendment Regulations, 2026, Scheme II paragraphs 10-11, Gazette English PDF pp.44-45; CRS Contact Us support/grievance fields.

claims.statement: DoT's ETA service describes ETA/self-declaration for commercial finished wireless products operating in de-licensed bands and expressly gives headphones/earphones as examples, subject to RF test and representative/manufacturer evidence.
claims.subject: WPC ETA conceptual scope
claims.applicability: Exact equipment using de-licensed bands within current rules; does not resolve the 2026 filing route
claims.locator: DoT eServices 'Equipment Type Approval (ETA)' page, description, eligibility and document sections, updated 28-05-2025.

claims.statement: The ETA service page still instructs submission through Saral Sanchar, while DoT's current notice says new Indian Telegraph Act applications stopped and Telecommunications Act 2023 authorisations/migrations use a new authorisation portal from 25 June 2026.
claims.subject: WPC application portal, fee and validity route
claims.applicability: New wireless authorisation/ETA application after the stated transition
claims.locator: ETA page 'Application Process' versus DoT Saral/WPC page banner 'Acceptance of new applications under Indian Telegraph Act stopped' and new portal date 25-06-2026.

claims.statement: The 2026 REPA Rules require an eligible person proposing to manufacture, purchase or import radio equipment for sale/hire/repair/test/demo to apply through the portal with activity, make/model and quantity and prescribed fee unless an exact rule 10 exception applies; rule 10 also says the excepted persons cannot manufacture, sell or hire that radio equipment.
claims.subject: Radio Equipment Possession Authorisation route and exceptions
claims.applicability: Possession/import of radio equipment for the listed commercial/test activities; exact exception and spectrum facts are case-specific
claims.locator: Telecommunications (Radio Equipment Possession Authorisation) Rules, 2026, rules 4-6 and 10, Gazette PDF pp.1-3 and 5-6; DoT REPA service page, eligibility, documents, fees, application steps, status and helpdesk sections.

claims.statement: REPA carries an INR 1,000 application fee; the authorisation fee is INR 10,000 per annum for manufacture/purchase/import for sale or hire and INR 2,000 per annum for repair/test/demo, prorated for a shorter period subject to an INR 500 minimum.
claims.subject: REPA statutory fees
claims.applicability: The stated activity and period under a REPA application/letter of intent
claims.locator: Telecommunications (Radio Equipment Possession Authorisation) Rules, 2026, rules 4(4) and 5(3), Gazette PDF pp.1-2.

claims.statement: A REPA grant for manufacture/purchase/import for sale or hire may be valid from one to five years; a grant for repair/test/demo may not exceed twelve months.
claims.subject: REPA validity
claims.applicability: Granted REPA; actual dates and conditions are those in the instrument
claims.locator: Telecommunications (Radio Equipment Possession Authorisation) Rules, 2026, rule 6, Gazette PDF p.3.

claims.statement: The current MTCTE portal states that notified telecom equipment cannot be sold, deployed or used without a Certificate of Conformity and provides the current product/essential-requirement and application route.
claims.subject: MTCTE scope
claims.applicability: Equipment within a current MTCTE notification
claims.locator: MTCTE portal home/About MTCTE text under the Telecommunications (Framework to Notify Standards, Conformity Assessment and Certification) Rules, 2025, accessed 28-08-2026.

claims.statement: The E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 apply to Schedule-I electrical/electronic equipment; a producer includes a person offering imported EEE under its brand or importing used EEE, and covered entities must register on the portal and not conduct covered business without registration.
claims.subject: E-waste scope and registration
claims.applicability: Only Schedule-I EEE and covered producer role; exact product mapping is separate
claims.locator: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, rules 2, 3(1)(t), 4 and 5, PDF pp.20-24; Schedule I at PDF pp.29-30.

claims.statement: CPCB's official e-waste guidance states that producers of Schedule-I EEE must register on the E-Waste EPR Portal; the public route does not by itself establish that a particular product is in Schedule I.
claims.subject: E-waste producer registration route
claims.applicability: Producer of exact Schedule-I EEE
claims.locator: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, rules 4-5; CPCB FAQ dated 23-01-2024, registration questions for Schedule-I EEE producers and E-Waste EPR Portal.

claims.statement: The Battery Waste Management Rules define producer to include import of a battery and equipment containing a battery, impose EPR, and require producer registration through the CPCB online central portal under the amended rule.
claims.subject: Battery EPR
claims.applicability: Importer/producer of batteries or equipment containing batteries within the Rules
claims.locator: Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, rule 3(1)(u) and rule 4; 2023 amendment substituting producer registration in rule 4; CPCB Battery EPR portal producer description.

claims.statement: Schedule I paragraph 2(ia) requires producers, on or before 31 March 2025, to ensure that all batteries or battery packs produced are appropriately marked with the EPR registration number issued under rule 4.
claims.subject: Battery EPR registration-number marking
claims.applicability: A producer, including the importer role established for equipment containing a battery; actual lot marking remains private user evidence
claims.locator: Battery Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2023, S.O. 4669(E), rule 10(b) inserting Schedule I paragraph 2(ia), official Gazette PDF pp.9-10.

claims.statement: Subject to providing information in writing to CPCB, a producer may satisfy paragraph 2(ia) by a barcode/QR code containing the EPR registration number on the battery/battery pack, equipment containing it, their packaging or eligible bulk packaging, or by printing the EPR registration number on the product information brochure.
claims.subject: Alternative placement for battery EPR registration number
claims.applicability: Producer choosing the Schedule I paragraph 2(ib) alternative; the Legal Metrology rule 26 packaging proviso and precise selected placement must be applied
claims.locator: Battery Waste Management Amendment Rules, 2025, S.O. 958(E), rule 2(b) inserting Schedule I paragraph 2(ib), official Gazette PDF pp.2-3.

claims.statement: CPCB's plastic EPR portal states that the old portal was discontinued on 28 June 2026 and data/users moved to the Common EPR Portal, using the existing authorised-person and company PAN identity.
claims.subject: Plastic EPR portal route
claims.applicability: Plastic EPR users/PIBO roles where the law applies
claims.locator: CPCB EPR Plastic Packaging portal landing notice, discontinuation/migration text dated 28-06-2026.

claims.statement: The Plastic Waste Management Schedule-II EPR Guidelines apply to pre-consumer and post-consumer plastic packaging and place EPR responsibility on producers, importers and brand owners, who must register through CPCB's online centralised portal; CPCB migrated plastic EPR users to the Common EPR Portal on 28 June 2026.
claims.subject: Plastic-packaging PIBO registration
claims.applicability: Actual producer/importer/brand-owner role and covered plastic-packaging category; packaging BOM and quantities are case evidence
claims.locator: Plastic Waste Management Rules Schedule II EPR Guidelines, paragraphs 1.3 and 10.1, official Gazette PDF; CPCB plastic portal migration notice dated 28-06-2026.

claims.statement: DGFT's import-policy notes preserve environmental restrictions/permissions for ODS, hazardous waste and hazardous chemicals in addition to other product controls.
claims.subject: Environmental import branches
claims.applicability: Goods with the identified environmental/hazardous trait
claims.locator: General Notes to Import Policy 2025, PDF pp.7-9, notes on ODS, hazardous waste and hazardous chemicals.

claims.statement: Imported retail packages within the Packaged Commodities Rules require the applicable manufacturer/packer/importer identity and address, country of origin, common/generic name, net quantity, date/best-before where applicable, MRP inclusive of taxes, consumer-care and other rule/product declarations.
claims.subject: Imported packaged commodities
claims.applicability: Packages within the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules; exemptions/product-specific declarations require separate review
claims.locator: DGFT General Notes to Import Policy 2025, PDF pp.5-6; Department of Consumer Affairs advisory dated 18-01-2023, rule 6 declaration summary for retail/inner packages.

claims.statement: The Department of Consumer Affairs' current Legal Metrology portal directs Rule 27 Packaged Commodities Registration applications to NSWS and provides a public certificate registry listing application, company, issue date and certificate number.
claims.subject: Legal Metrology registration route and proof
claims.applicability: Rule 27 registration where the Department/competent jurisdiction accepts the NSWS route
claims.locator: Legal Metrology landing page current Rule 27 NSWS direction and support email; Packaged Commodities Registration Certificates registry columns, accessed 28-08-2026.

claims.statement: DGFT's current General Notes identify conditional import branches for BIS-notified goods, electronics/IT, plant quarantine/SPS, food, GM products, environmental/hazardous goods, livestock and other specially controlled categories; each branch requires the exact operative rule and product facts.
claims.subject: Sector-regulator discovery
claims.applicability: Only where the exact product/trait falls within the cited branch
claims.locator: General Notes to Import Policy 2025, PDF pp.2-11, notes on BIS/electronics, plant quarantine, food, GM, environment/hazardous, livestock and other special categories.

claims.statement: The official GST tutorials route new registration through Services > Registration > New Registration, provide an online clarification response path, and allow download of the registration certificate after grant; actual liability and State/UT remain fact-dependent.
claims.subject: GST registration portal
claims.applicability: Person determined to require GST registration
claims.locator: GST Portal official tutorials: Aadhaar Authentication/New Registration navigation; Application for Filing Clarification; View/Download Certificates.

claims.statement: A person who is liable to register must apply in every State or Union territory in which liable within thirty days from the date liability arose; whether liability arose, the State/UT and any exception remain fact-specific.
claims.subject: GST registration application timing
claims.applicability: Person established as liable under the current CGST/SGST framework
claims.locator: CGST Act, 2017, section 25(1), current CBIC Tax Information Portal consolidated text.

claims.statement: A registered person supplying taxable goods issues a tax invoice before or at removal/delivery, and rule 46 prescribes invoice particulars; the exact product rate, supply treatment and invoice instance remain case evidence.
claims.subject: GST first-sale tax invoice
claims.applicability: Registered person making a taxable supply of goods
claims.locator: CGST Act, 2017, section 31(1); CGST Rules, rule 46, current CBIC Tax Information Portal consolidated text.

claims.statement: Import IGST credit requires a registered person's business-use eligibility and statutory conditions including possession of prescribed tax document, receipt, tax payment and return; Rule 36 identifies the Bill of Entry or similar customs document as an eligible document.
claims.subject: GST input tax credit on imports
claims.applicability: Registered person seeking otherwise eligible import IGST credit
claims.locator: CGST Act, 2017, Section 16(1)-(2); CGST Rules, Rule 36(1)(d), current CBIC Tax Information Portal text.

claims.statement: For the bounded over-ear Bluetooth-headphone demo, DGFT's current ITC(HS) table shows 851830 subentries including 85183011 (TWS), 85183019 (Other) and 85183020 (wired headphones only), with Free policy in the table, but the exact subheading for the stated product is not admitted without full tariff-note analysis.
claims.subject: Demo tariff classification
claims.applicability: Only the bounded demo product facts; not other headphones/electronics
claims.locator: DGFT Notification ITC(HS) PDF, heading 851830 table and subentries 85183011/85183019/85183020; classification analysis and notes not completed to a binding result.

claims.statement: The actual sale/storage/premises model can create State/UT or municipal permissions, and alcohol imports specifically remain subject to State Government requirements; no single national local-licence procedure is supportable without location and product facts.
claims.subject: State/local dependencies
claims.applicability: Depends on product, premises, employees, activity, supply and State/UT
claims.locator: DGFT General Notes to Import Policy 2025, alcohol note on State Government requirements; GST registration clarification tutorial contains state-specific information routing. Broader premises dependencies require direct local verification.

claims.statement: Because imports remain subject to domestic product/environment/safety law and BIS/other regimes can prohibit manufacture, import, sale or distribution without conformity, Customs Out of Charge alone is not sufficient evidence for legal sale.
claims.subject: Final sale gate
claims.applicability: Regulated imported products
claims.locator: DGFT General Notes opening and BIS notes; BIS compulsory certification page; CRS 'What is CRS' prohibition on manufacture/store for sale/import/sell/distribute notified goods without conformity.

conflicts.description: The official ETA page still directs Saral Sanchar, while DoT's current transition notice moves new Telecommunications Act authorisations to the Authorisation Portal from 25 June 2026. This conflict is confined to ETA; the separate REPA service and rule-10 exceptions are current and verified.
conflicts.safe_treatment: Treat only the ETA application URL, fee, timeline and legacy validity language as unresolved; separately close REPA under task imp.t09a and do not dispatch until every applicable radio gate is evidenced.
conflicts.resolution_owner_action: Importer must get written WPC/DoT confirmation of the exact ETA service/portal for the model/configuration.

conflicts.description: Single-window availability is national in concept, but the Plant Quarantine replacement of separate PQMS filing is phased by port/readiness.
conflicts.safe_treatment: Do not choose or omit PQMS/SWIFT filing until the intended port confirms current rollout.
conflicts.resolution_owner_action: Importer/customs broker must confirm the route with the relevant Plant Quarantine station and ICEGATE for the shipment date.

coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: A complete model-level classification analysis applying the current tariff text, notes and alternatives; the demo subheading is not final. The public CAAR route is now verified, but no case ruling exists.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not declare a code, policy status or rate as final; block dispatch if material ambiguity remains.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Complete the technical dossier and reasoned tariff analysis; if ambiguity is material, submit Form CAAR-1 to the regulation-6 jurisdictional Authority and obtain the signed ruling before relying on it.

coverage_gaps.topic: Current duty, exemption, trade remedy and preference
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Exact classification, origin, shipment date, value additions, current notifications and preference documents.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Withhold every numeric duty/rate/exemption/landed-cost claim and use only the shipment assessment for payment.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Run a dated line-level tariff/notification/remedy/origin review and reconcile to customs assessment.

coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: An authoritative ETA-specific mapping from the legacy Saral instruction to the exact new Telecommunications Act service and URL. REPA is no longer part of this gap.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not file ETA through an assumed legacy route or import/sell radio goods on a pending/unverified ETA; independently close the verified REPA branch.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Obtain written WPC/DoT ETA confirmation for the exact model, frequencies, applicant and import purpose.

coverage_gaps.topic: Exact radio spectrum eligibility, REPA exception match and other WPC licences
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Production radio parameters matched to current spectrum exemptions and the demo's exact rule-10 REPA exception/authorisation facts; the current REPA portal, fees, validity and statutory exception classes are verified.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not infer a commercial-import exception from licence-exempt spectrum or end-user status; keep all unmatched radio gates Action Required.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Collect RF and existing-authorisation evidence, apply current spectrum notifications and REPA rules 4/10, then obtain the grant or written WPC clarification.

coverage_gaps.topic: BIS shipment model/factory licence scope and authenticated application state
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: A Form V licence and active public record matching the actual manufacturer, factory, brand, model, standard and validity; if applying/remediating, the private notice, response and logged-in state. Public search, suspension/cancellation duties and support/grievance routes are verified.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: A lab report, application receipt, grievance or certificate for another model/factory cannot support dispatch or sale; negative status invokes task imp.t08a.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Apply under current Scheme II, obtain Form V, verify the public record and close any notice through BIS; retain a current matching record before dispatch.

coverage_gaps.topic: E-waste Schedule-I mapping for the demo headphones
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: A current authoritative mapping of the exact headphones to a Schedule-I EEE category and the user's authenticated registration state; the producer-registration route is now verified.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not claim exemption or registration completion; block sale if coverage remains unresolved.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Submit exact product/category facts to CPCB or obtain a qualified current-rule opinion; if covered, complete task imp.t11b and retain the granted category-matched certificate.

coverage_gaps.topic: Plastic packaging EPR case applicability and authenticated state
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Exact package material/quantity, PIBO role/category and logged-in Common EPR application/fee/status. The governing PIBO registration obligation and current Common Portal route are verified.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not infer non-applicability from low quantity, packaging supplier involvement or public-login availability.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Complete the packaging BOM/PIBO assessment, submit the role/category application through Common EPR and retain the granted registration/current controls.

coverage_gaps.topic: GST case liability, rate and return profile
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Entity turnover, date liability arose, State/UT locations, supply channels/buyers, product classification/rate and current registration/return facts. Section-25 application timing and section-31/rule-46 invoice baseline are verified.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not assert universal liability, threshold, rate or return conclusions and do not claim import credit until conditions are evidenced.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Complete tax/location facts, establish liability/date and product/supply treatment, apply in each relevant State/UT and validate the actual invoice/return configuration.

coverage_gaps.topic: Legal Metrology case jurisdiction, exemptions, fee and timing
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Current product/package exemptions, competent Central versus State authority, package/channel facts, fee/timing and authenticated NSWS case state. The current NSWS route, public certificate proof and declaration baseline are verified.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Quarantine pre-packaged stock and withhold artwork release until the competent jurisdiction, registration and full exact checklist are closed.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Confirm jurisdiction/current exemptions with Legal Metrology, apply through the verified route where applicable and validate the granted certificate plus physical/online artwork.

coverage_gaps.topic: Other product-sector regulator and pre-import permit
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Product-neutral research cannot decide FSSAI/CDSCO/biosecurity/wildlife/chemical/PESO/BEE/pesticide/other scope without exact product traits and use.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Any selected or unknown regulated trait blocks dispatch and sale.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Map the exact trait to the operative notification, competent authority, pre-import permit, port and shipment NOC route.

coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Final Indian port, referral/PGA and live rollout status, especially phased Plant Quarantine SWIFT/PQMS implementation.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not assume a standalone portal is retired or a chosen port is designated/ready.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Confirm current route with ICEGATE and the competent PGA station before booking and filing.

coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Actual State/UT, municipality, premises, employees, product, storage risk and sales channels.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not represent the business as sale-ready at an unidentified location.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Identify every premises/activity and verify only with the competent State/UT/municipal authorities; build a local matrix.

coverage_gaps.topic: Private and regulated-actor costs, schedules and document performance
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Chosen broker/carrier/lab/custodian/bank, route, quotes, storage days, examination and service terms.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not promise private fees or transit/clearance time and keep contingency before ordering/booking.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Verify actor authority/accreditation, obtain scoped quotes and reconcile actual documents/status for the shipment.

coverage_gaps.topic: Statutory filing/payment/remediation deadlines for the actual route
coverage_gaps.missing_evidence: Shipment mode/arrival date, port, assessment/notice text and exact applicable amended provision/instrument. Current acknowledgement/query/status/export/helpdesk routes are verified but do not supply the case deadline.
coverage_gaps.safe_treatment: Do not use a generic day count; check before arrival and calendar each case-specific deadline immediately.
coverage_gaps.resolution_path: Apply current Customs Act/rules/advisory and the actual query/notice/licence conditions with qualified review; use the verified ICEGATE message/status records as the dated trigger evidence.

demo_scenario.title: Bounded demo: first sea shipment of new over-ear Bluetooth headphones
demo_scenario.purpose: Exercise the generic graph against a representative regulated electronics shipment while preserving unresolved legal gates and without turning the graph into a headphone-only workflow.
assumptions: Indian private limited company is importer of record and will make ordinary commercial retail/e-commerce sales from one identified State after customs clearance.
New finished over-ear Bluetooth-only headphones, not true-wireless earbuds, with an integrated rechargeable lithium battery and no charger in the box.
Foreign manufacturer and factory are known; goods are made in and shipped by sea from China under an ordinary purchase, not related-party, used, sample, repair, waste or preferential-origin claim.
Bluetooth radio only; no cellular, satellite, drone, radar, jammer, medical, telecom-network or safety-critical function.
Retail pre-package includes plastic packaging; product is not food, drug, cosmetic, medical device, plant, animal, wildlife, alcohol, tobacco, pesticide, hazardous chemical or ODS.
Exact model, radio parameters, tariff notes, values, port, approvals, labels and State location remain user evidence to be supplied and verified.

qualifier_answers.answer: New finished over-ear Bluetooth headphones; exact model-level technical dossier still required.
Bluetooth only; exact frequency/power/module/antenna evidence remains Action Required.
Assumed consumer accessory only, but current MTCTE notified-list check remains required.
None of the listed food/health/biosecurity/hazardous traits on stated assumptions; still subject to regulator-matrix review.
Integrated rechargeable battery, electrical/electronic equipment and plastic retail packaging.
Yes, imported in retail pre-package for retail and e-commerce sale.
Indian private limited importer; matching PAN/bank/IEC/GSTIN/ICEGATE evidence not yet supplied.
Sea shipment from China under ordinary purchase; exact commercial values, Incoterm, origin evidence, route and port not yet supplied.
Candidate 851830 family and table shows Free subentries, but exact subheading/policy conditions are not final.
One identified State and retail/e-commerce sales assumed; GST facts/rate/invoicing remain Action Required.
No certificate is accepted until holder/factory/brand/model/standard/validity match the shipment.

out_of_scope_facts: No numeric duty, GST rate, private charge, shipment time or customs deadline is assumed.
No preferential tariff claim, related-party valuation, repair/sample exemption, used-goods path or restricted-goods authorisation is assumed.
No charger/power adapter, spare battery, cellular radio, other bundled model or accessory is covered by the demo's product facts.
No specific State/UT, port, warehouse, marketplace or municipal procedure is selected.
No FSSAI, CDSCO, plant/animal/wildlife, hazardous, ODS, BEE, PESO or other sector path is triggered by the bounded assumptions.
action_required_gates: Final tariff subheading and all current duty/exemption/trade-remedy/origin inputs.

Active BIS Scheme-II Form V coverage for Wireless Headphone and Earphone under the current standard, matching the exact manufacturer/factory/brand/model; the 2026 Regulations control application evidence, fees, validity and negative-status response, but any actual notice/suspension/cancellation must close through task imp.t08a.

Exact Bluetooth spectrum eligibility and written confirmation of the post-June-2026 ETA route; separately obtain REPA or prove an exact rule-10 exception permitting commercial import/sale under task imp.t09a.
Current MTCTE notified-product check; retain a sourced non-applicability decision if it is only a consumer accessory.

Battery producer registration is expected on the stated integrated-battery facts, and the actual sale lot must separately prove the correct EPR registration-number marking or the written-to-CPCB 2025 barcode/QR/brochure alternative; exact e-waste Schedule-I mapping and plastic-packaging BOM/PIBO case evidence remain unresolved under tasks imp.t11b and imp.t11c even though their public registration routes are verified.
Legal Metrology competent jurisdiction, NSWS/competent registration and complete physical/e-commerce declarations for the exact package.

GST actual liability, State/UT, rate, return, invoice and credit facts plus actual State/UT/local premises permissions; section-25 timing and section-31/rule-46 invoice baseline do not decide those case facts.
Final port/PGA review, controlled documents, Bill of Entry assessment, payment, required NOCs and Customs Out of Charge.
Lot-level final sale release; Customs Out of Charge alone is insufficient.
demo_scenario.non_universality_note: This scenario is a bounded test fixture. Its Bluetooth/BIS/battery/package branches and non-triggered sector assumptions must never be reused for another model or product without re-answering all qualifiers and rerunning the generic graph.
